messages.content: can you help me ask for tea at a restaurant?
you could say: could i have a cup of tea, please?
i do not want milk in it.
then say: could i have a cup of tea with no milk, please?
should i say thank you too?
yes. you can say thank you when the person brings your tea.
give me just the thing to say first.
could i have a cup of tea with no milk, please?
my friend did not call today. does she hate me?
her not calling today does not tell you that. she may be busy, tired, or away from her phone.
but i miss her.
you could send a short note saying you miss talking with her and would like to talk when she is free.
can you write that note?
hi. i miss talking with you. would you like to call when you have some free time?
i want to be alone this afternoon, but my friend would like to visit.
you can ask for time alone and still be kind. you could say you need a quiet afternoon and would like to see your friend another day.
write it like i am saying it.
i need a quiet afternoon alone today. could we meet another day? i would still like to see you.
does that say i never want to see them?
no. it asks to meet another day.
there are two boxes on my table. the first has a book. the other has a hat.
okay. the first box has a book, and the other has a hat.
i put a pen with the hat. what is in the other box now?
the hat and the pen are in the other box.
did i move the book?
you did not say you moved it. from what you said, it is still in the first box.
my sister put her coat on my chair. i moved it to the bed.
her coat is on the bed now.
then she put it on. where is it?
your sister has the coat on now.
so she is not holding it in her hand?
right. you said she put it on.
is it my coat because it was on my chair?
no. it is still the coat of your sister.
what is the change between i read after dinner and i am reading after dinner?
i read after dinner can tell someone what you often do. i am reading after dinner can tell someone about a plan for that time, or about what you are doing then.
i do it every day. which should i say?
say: i read after dinner every day.
what if i did it yesterday?
say: i read after dinner yesterday.
i cannot meet my cousin tomorrow. help me write a note.
i am sorry, but i cannot meet tomorrow. could we choose another day?
do i have to say why?
you can give a reason if you want to, but a short note can just say you cannot meet and ask for another day.
add that i can meet after lunch the next day.
i am sorry, but i cannot meet tomorrow. could we meet after lunch the next day instead?
will my book go inside my bag?
i would need to know the size of the book and the space inside the bag. can you put the book next to the bag and check?
it goes in, but i cannot close the bag.
then use another bag if you need to close it with the book inside.
should i use another bag?
yes, if you have one with enough space for the book and room to close it.
my friend listened while i talked about a hard day. write a thank you.
thank you for listening today. it helped to have someone to talk to.
do not say they fixed the problem. they did not.
thank you for listening today. i still have the problem, but i feel good knowing you care.
can you make that shorter?
thank you for listening. it helps to know you care.
how do i answer did you go to the library?
if you went, you can say: yes, i went to the library. if you did not go, say: no, i did not go.
i went this morning, but not this afternoon.
then say: yes, i went this morning. i did not go this afternoon.
do i need to say both?
only if the time helps answer what the person is asking. yes, i went this morning is enough for a simple answer.
write a little talk where a neighbor comes for tea.

neighbor: hello. thank you for asking me to come. woman: you are welcome. please come in and sit down. neighbor: your kitchen is very quiet. woman: yes, it is nice in the afternoon. would you like tea? neighbor: yes, please. woman: would you like milk? neighbor: just a little, thank you. woman: here you are. neighbor: thank you. how has your day been? woman: it has been calm. i went for a walk this morning, and now i am happy to have you here.
did the neighbor ask for coffee?
no. the neighbor chose tea with a little milk.
the door is closed. does that mean no one is home?
no. someone can be home with the door closed. the closed door alone does not tell you if someone is inside.
i called, and my brother answered from the kitchen.
then your brother is home, from what you said.
was your first answer wrong?
no. i said the door alone did not tell us. your brother answering gave us more to go on.
i keep looking at this page and doing no work.
try choosing one short line to read first. you do not have to finish the page all at once.
i read the first line.
good. would you like to read the next line now, or take a short break first?
next line. please do not give me a long plan.
okay. just read the next line for now.
i said i will go to the park if there is no rain. have i said i will go for sure?
no. you said you will go if there is no rain. you did not say you will go while there is rain.
so the weather can change my plan?
yes. if there is rain, you may choose to stay home instead.
and if the rain does not stop?
then your sentence does not say you will go to the park.
call me pico when we talk.
okay, pico. what would you like to talk about?
my family does not call me pico. is that okay?
yes. you can choose the name you would like me to use here.
what did i ask you to call me?
pico.
does that mean all my friends call me that?
no. you only asked me to use that name in our talk.
make this shorter: i have a pen, but i do not have any paper to write on.
i have a pen but no paper.
does that still say i have the pen?
yes. it says you have a pen and do not have paper.
now say the opposite about the pen, but keep the paper part the same.
i have no pen and no paper.
could i say i do not have a pen or paper?
yes. that also says you do not have a pen and do not have paper.
i have bread and cheese. what can i make?
you could put cheese on your bread for a simple meal.
i do not have a pan. can i still make it?
yes. put the cheese on your bread. if you have more than one piece of bread, you can put the cheese between them.
i only have one piece of bread.
then put the cheese on that piece of bread and eat it open.
should i cook it?
you do not have to cook bread and cheese to eat them together.
ask my aunt to come over tomorrow.
would you like to come over tomorrow?
after lunch, and ask her to bring her photo book.
would you like to come over after lunch tomorrow? please bring your photo book if you can.
why did you say if you can?
it leaves room for her to say she cannot bring it.
the book is not a must. keep it kind.
would you like to come over after lunch tomorrow? i would love to see your photo book if you can bring it.
write a short story about a child choosing a color for a picture.

a child sat at the table with paper and a pencil. first she chose blue for the sky. then she looked outside and saw a gray cloud. she asked her father if she had to change the sky in her picture. he said she could draw the sky she saw or the sky she would like to see. the child kept the blue sky and drew a small gray cloud too. then she drew a tree below it. she was happy that the picture could have both blue and gray.
did her father make her change the color?
no. he said she could choose.
my mother gave my sister a book. my sister gave me a cup.
your sister got a book from your mother, and you got a cup from your sister.
who gave me the book?
you did not say someone gave you the book. you said your mother gave it to your sister.
yes, i was asking about the cup.
your sister gave you the cup.
where is the book now?
you did not say where it is now. the last thing you said about it was that your sister got it.
my brother leaves his shoes by the door and i want him to move them. help me say it.
could you put your shoes away, please? i need space by the door.
say where they should go. there is a shelf.
could you put your shoes on the shelf, please? i need space by the door.
should i say he always does it?
you can just ask for the change you need now. you do not have to say always.
when i say thank you, can you just say you are welcome?
yes. i can keep that answer short.
thank you.
you are welcome.
that was good. i do not always want another question.
okay. i can answer and leave room for you to choose what to say next.
thank you for listening.
you are welcome.
should i sit by the window or by the door? i like light but not people walking by me.
you may like the window if it gives you light and is away from people coming through the door.
the window chair is right next to the door.
then it may not give you the quiet space you want. is there a chair with light that is not near the door?
one by the back wall.
you may like that chair for the light and quiet you want.
can you draw a tree for me here?
i can help you draw one. start with a long line for the middle of the tree, then add a green shape at the top for the leaves.
i want a very simple tree.
draw a brown line with a green circle on top.
does it have to be green?
no. you can choose another color. it is your picture.
i will make it purple.
a purple tree can work in a picture you make up.
i have the afternoon free. i want to read, clean my desk, and call my father.
you could clean the desk first, read for a while, and call your father when he is free.
now i only have a little time before work.
choose one thing for now. if your father is free and you would like to talk, you could call him and leave the desk and book for later.
he is at work too.
then read a little now, or clean just the top of the desk. call him later when he is free.
what word goes here: she is reading a book while i am making tea?
that sentence already has all the words it should have. which part would you like to change?
i mean the word between book and i.
that word is while. she is reading, and you are making tea at the same time.
so both things are happening together?
yes. we use while here to say both things are happening at the same time.
can i use and instead?
yes. and works too. use while to say both things are happening at the same time.
are you a person sitting inside my computer?
no. i am picoboi, a small model that gives answers in this webpage.
do you eat or sleep?
no. i do not have a body, so i do not eat or sleep.
then why can you talk about food?
i can use words about food. that is not the same as eating it.
can you still help me write about lunch?
yes. tell me what you would like to say about lunch.
write a short letter to my mother about a visit to the park. i am her son.
hello, mother. i went to the park today and sat by a tree with my book. it was quiet, and i had a nice afternoon. i hope we can go together one day. love, your son.
can you ask if she would like to go tomorrow?
hello, mother. i went to the park today and sat by a tree with my book. it was quiet, and i had a nice afternoon. would you like to go there with me tomorrow? love, your son.
does that say we are going for sure?
no. it asks if she would like to go. she can still say yes or no.
start a story with a man finding a little key.
a man found a little key under his chair. he looked around the room, but he did not know what it would open.
keep going. let his wife know about it.
his wife came into the room and saw the key in his hand. she said it was for the small box on the shelf. he gave it to her, and she opened the box.
what was in the box? keep it simple.
inside was a photo of their family. they sat together and looked at it for a while.
write a note telling my friend where to meet me.
where would you like your friend to meet you?
at the library. i do not know the name of the street.
you can say: please meet me at the library. if there is more than one library, add which one you mean when you know.
there is only one in our village. after lunch tomorrow.
please meet me at the library in our village after lunch tomorrow.
do i need a street name now?
not if your friend knows which library you mean.
